title: Travel insurance premium factors
scenario: Every new risk factor (age, adventure sports, destination) means editing one giant premium class.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · Spring MVC · List<T> injection · @Order · @Qualifier · @Primary · @PostConstruct · MockMvc
simulation: A quote only: no policy is issued and nothing is charged. The rates are demo numbers, not a real insurer's, and taxes are not included.

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. One giant premium class

    Every new risk (a new destination, a new age band, adventure sports) means editing the same 400-line class. Every edit risks every price.

  2. A first split goes wrong

    Factors become separate beans, but the quote service asks for one PremiumFactor. The app will not start; someone adds @Primary, and it starts, quoting with one factor. Then the order of the factors depends on how classes were scanned, and the adventure loading gets multiplied by age: ₹400 too much.

  3. The fix

    Inject all factors as a list, in an explicit order, and refuse to start if two share an order.

When several beans do one job together, ask for all of them, and say their order out loud.

What are we building?

POST /premium-quotes prices a trip by running every premium factor in order, and returns the premium with a breakdown of each step.

An everyday analogy

A recipe: dough, then filling, then oven, then glaze. Each step is separate and numbered. Swap the oven and the glaze and you get a different dish, from the same ingredients.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. At startup, Spring collects every PremiumFactor bean, sorted by @Order, and the calculator checks no two share a place.
  2. For each quote, the running total starts at zero.
  3. Each factor takes the total and returns a new one, with a line for the breakdown.
  4. Finally, the premium is rounded up to the rupee (the insurer's rule) and the per-day figure to the nearest rupee.
Check yourself: the adventure add-on is ₹50 a day. Why does it matter whether it comes before or after the age multiplier?

After, it stays ₹50 a day. Before, it is multiplied too: ×1.8 for a 67-year-old, ₹90 a day. Same factors, different price, so the order is part of the rule.

What this station is not

  • Not real insurance pricing. Demo rates; real pricing is regulated and actuarial.
  • No policy. A quote only.
  • No taxes. The premium shown excludes them.

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Bimaly (a fictional insurance app) adds risk factors often. In one class, each change risks every price; split carelessly into beans, the app either fails to start, quotes with one factor, or applies factors in whatever order classes happen to load.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Given age 67, Europe, 10 days, adventure sports, then ₹1,838.75 before rounding, charged as ₹1,839, with base, destination, age, adventure and minimum in that order.
  2. Given age 25, Asia, 3 days, then the ₹199 minimum.
  3. Given age 45, Europe, 5 days, then ₹483.44 is charged as ₹484: rounded up, never to the nearest.
  4. Given age 81, then 422: online quotes go up to 80 (a demo rule).
  5. Given an unknown destination, days outside 1 to 180, or no age, then 400.
  6. Given two factors with the same @Order, or one with none, then the app does not start.

Requirements

  • Demo rates: ₹42.50 a day; destination ×1.00 to ×3.00; age ×0.80 to ×2.50; adventure +₹50 a day, not multiplied; minimum ₹199.
  • Each step rounds to the paisa; the premium rounds up to the rupee; the per-day figure to the nearest rupee.
  • Factors are stateless singletons; a new factor is a new bean with an @Order.
  • adventureSports is optional (false when missing).

Learning objectives

  • Inject several beans of one type as a List, in a defined order.
  • Choose one bean among several with @Qualifier, and a default with @Primary.
  • Know why factors must be stateless singletons.
  • Use a lifecycle callback (@PostConstruct) to fail fast at startup.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Injecting one bean when several exist, or relying on unspecified bean order.

The first test builds a small context where a service asks for one PremiumFactor among two: it does not start. The second adds @Primary to one, the usual quick fix: it starts, and quotes a free policy, because only the age factor runs. The third applies the same five factors in two orders: ₹1,838.75 against ₹2,238.75. While building, removing @Order from one factor stopped the app (the startup check), moving adventure before age turned 2 tests red, and dropping the @Qualifier from the calculator turned 1 red (₹483 instead of ₹484).

package com.bimaly.premiums;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.runner.ApplicationContextRunner;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Primary;

import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

/** The first test written for this station: it reproduces both ways the old wiring went wrong. */
class FactorOrderTrapTest {

    static final Trip SENIOR_IN_EUROPE = new Trip(67, Trip.Destination.EUROPE, 10, true);

    /** The "before" quote service: one factor, injected by type. Kept only in tests. */
    record OldQuoteService(PremiumFactor factor) {
        long quote(Trip trip) {
            return factor.apply(trip, 0).totalPaise();
        }
    }

    @Configuration
    static class TwoFactorsOneConsumer {
        @Bean
        PremiumFactor base() {
            return new Factors.Base();
        }

        @Bean
        PremiumFactor age() {
            return new Factors.Age();
        }

        @Bean
        OldQuoteService oldQuoteService(PremiumFactor factor) {
            return new OldQuoteService(factor);
        }
    }

    @Configuration
    static class SomeoneAddedPrimary {
        @Bean
        PremiumFactor base() {
            return new Factors.Base();
        }

        @Bean
        @Primary
        PremiumFactor age() {
            return new Factors.Age();
        }

        @Bean
        OldQuoteService oldQuoteService(PremiumFactor factor) {
            return new OldQuoteService(factor);
        }
    }

    static long applyInOrder(List<PremiumFactor> factors, Trip trip) {
        long total = 0;
        for (PremiumFactor f : factors) {
            total = f.apply(trip, total).totalPaise();
        }
        return total;
    }

    @Test
    void oneInjectedFactorAmongSeveralStopsTheAppStarting() {
        new ApplicationContextRunner().withUserConfiguration(TwoFactorsOneConsumer.class)
                .run(context -> assertThat(context).hasFailed().getFailure().rootCause().isInstanceOf(NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.class));
    }

    @Test
    void theQuickFixWithPrimaryStartsAndQuotesWithOneFactorOnly() {
        new ApplicationContextRunner().withUserConfiguration(SomeoneAddedPrimary.class).run(context -> {
            assertThat(context).hasNotFailed();
            assertThat(context.getBean(OldQuoteService.class).quote(SENIOR_IN_EUROPE)).isZero();   // age x nothing: a free policy
        });
    }

    @Test
    void theOrderOfTheFactorsChangesThePrice() {
        List<PremiumFactor> right = List.of(new Factors.Base(), new Factors.DestinationRisk(), new Factors.Age(), new Factors.AdventureSports(), new Factors.Minimum());
        List<PremiumFactor> scanned = List.of(new Factors.Base(), new Factors.DestinationRisk(), new Factors.AdventureSports(), new Factors.Age(), new Factors.Minimum());
        assertThat(applyInOrder(right, SENIOR_IN_EUROPE)).isEqualTo(183_875);
        assertThat(applyInOrder(scanned, SENIOR_IN_EUROPE)).isEqualTo(223_875);   // the adventure loading multiplied by age: Rs 400 more
    }
}

package com.bimaly.premiums;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
class PremiumQuoteController {

    /** Oldest age we quote online (a demo rule); older travellers are referred to an agent. */
    static final int MAX_ONLINE_AGE = 80;

    record QuoteRequest(@NotNull @Min(0) @Max(120) Integer age, @NotNull Trip.Destination destination,
                        @NotNull @Min(1) @Max(180) Integer days, Boolean adventureSports) {
        // Boolean, not boolean: the field is optional, and Jackson 3 rejects a missing primitive (FAIL_ON_NULL_FOR_PRIMITIVES)
    }

    private final PremiumCalculator calculator;

    PremiumQuoteController(PremiumCalculator calculator) {
        this.calculator = calculator;
    }

    /** A quote only: no policy is issued and nothing is charged. */
    @PostMapping("/premium-quotes")
    PremiumCalculator.Quote quote(@Valid @RequestBody QuoteRequest r) {
        if (r.age() > MAX_ONLINE_AGE) {
            ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                    "Online quotes cover travellers up to " + MAX_ONLINE_AGE + ". An agent can quote for older travellers.");
            p.setTitle("No online cover for this age");
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, p, null);
        }
        return calculator.quote(new Trip(r.age(), r.destination(), r.days(), Boolean.TRUE.equals(r.adventureSports())));
    }
}

src/main/java/com/bimaly/premiums/PremiumCalculator.java

Does
Runs every factor in order, then rounds.
Why
List<PremiumFactor> from Spring, sorted by @Order; a new factor does not change this class.
Without it
The trap: one injected factor, or an order nobody chose.
  • @Qualifier("premium") picks the rounding that charges; the unqualified one is the @Primary.
  • @PostConstruct checks the orders once, after injection, before any quote.
package com.bimaly.premiums;

import jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Qualifier;
import org.springframework.core.annotation.AnnotationUtils;
import org.springframework.core.annotation.Order;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Runs every factor in order. Spring injects all PremiumFactor beans as one List, sorted by @Order. A new factor is a
 * new @Component with an @Order: this class does not change.
 */
@Service
class PremiumCalculator {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(PremiumCalculator.class);

    record Quote(long premiumPaise, long perDayPaise, List<PremiumFactor.Step> breakdown) {
    }

    private final List<PremiumFactor> factors;
    private final Rounding chargeRounding;
    private final Rounding displayRounding;

    PremiumCalculator(List<PremiumFactor> factors, @Qualifier("premium") Rounding chargeRounding, Rounding displayRounding) {
        this.factors = factors;
        this.chargeRounding = chargeRounding;
        this.displayRounding = displayRounding;   // no qualifier: the @Primary one
    }

    /**
     * Lifecycle callback: runs once, after injection, before the first quote. Refuses to start if a factor has no
     * @Order or shares one, because then the order, and so the price, would depend on how classes were scanned.
     */
    @PostConstruct
    void checkOrder() {
        Set<Integer> seen = new HashSet<>();
        for (PremiumFactor f : factors) {
            Order order = AnnotationUtils.findAnnotation(f.getClass(), Order.class);
            if (order == null || !seen.add(order.value())) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("Premium factor " + f.getClass().getSimpleName()
                        + (order == null ? " has no @Order" : " shares @Order(" + order.value() + ") with another factor"));
            }
        }
        log.info("Premium factors, in order: {}", factors.stream().map(f -> f.getClass().getSimpleName()).toList());
    }

    Quote quote(Trip trip) {
        long total = 0;
        List<PremiumFactor.Step> steps = new ArrayList<>();
        for (PremiumFactor f : factors) {
            PremiumFactor.Step step = f.apply(trip, total);
            steps.add(step);
            total = step.totalPaise();
        }
        long premium = chargeRounding.toRupee(total);
        return new Quote(premium, displayRounding.toRupee(premium / trip.days()), steps);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/bimaly/premiums/Factors.java

Does
The five factors, each a bean with its @Order.
Why
Small, stateless, independently testable steps.
Without it
One class that knows every rate.
package com.bimaly.premiums;

import org.springframework.core.annotation.Order;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.RoundingMode;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * The premium factors (demo rates, not a real insurer's). Order is part of the rule: multipliers apply to the cover
 * cost, the adventure loading is a flat add-on that is not multiplied by age, and the minimum is checked last.
 */
final class Factors {

    private Factors() {
    }

    static long times(long paise, String multiplier) {
        return BigDecimal.valueOf(paise).multiply(new BigDecimal(multiplier)).setScale(0, RoundingMode.HALF_UP).longValueExact();
    }

    static String rupees(long paise) {
        return BigDecimal.valueOf(paise, 2).toPlainString();
    }

    @Component
    @Order(10)
    static class Base implements PremiumFactor {
        static final long PER_DAY_PAISE = 4_250;

        public Step apply(Trip trip, long total) {
            long base = PER_DAY_PAISE * trip.days();
            return new Step("base", trip.days() + " days at Rs " + rupees(PER_DAY_PAISE), base);
        }
    }

    @Component
    @Order(20)
    static class DestinationRisk implements PremiumFactor {
        static final Map<Trip.Destination, String> MULTIPLIER = Map.of(Trip.Destination.ASIA, "1.00", Trip.Destination.EUROPE, "1.75",
                Trip.Destination.USA_CANADA, "2.75", Trip.Destination.WORLDWIDE, "3.00");

        public Step apply(Trip trip, long total) {
            String m = MULTIPLIER.get(trip.destination());
            return new Step("destination", trip.destination() + " x " + m, times(total, m));
        }
    }

    @Component
    @Order(30)
    static class Age implements PremiumFactor {
        public Step apply(Trip trip, long total) {
            String m = trip.age() < 18 ? "0.80" : trip.age() <= 40 ? "1.00" : trip.age() <= 60 ? "1.30" : trip.age() <= 70 ? "1.80" : "2.50";
            return new Step("age", "age " + trip.age() + " x " + m, times(total, m));
        }
    }

    @Component
    @Order(40)
    static class AdventureSports implements PremiumFactor {
        static final long PER_DAY_PAISE = 5_000;

        public Step apply(Trip trip, long total) {
            if (!trip.adventureSports()) {
                return new Step("adventure", "no adventure sports", total);
            }
            return new Step("adventure", "adventure sports, Rs " + rupees(PER_DAY_PAISE) + " a day", total + PER_DAY_PAISE * trip.days());
        }
    }

    @Component
    @Order(100)
    static class Minimum implements PremiumFactor {
        static final long MINIMUM_PAISE = 19_900;

        public Step apply(Trip trip, long total) {
            return total >= MINIMUM_PAISE ? new Step("minimum", "above the Rs 199.00 minimum", total)
                    : new Step("minimum", "raised to the Rs 199.00 minimum", MINIMUM_PAISE);
        }
    }
}

src/main/java/com/bimaly/premiums/PremiumFactor.java

The interface every factor implements, and the breakdown step it returns.

package com.bimaly.premiums;

/**
 * One step of the premium: takes the running total (paise) and returns the new one, with a line for the breakdown.
 * Each factor is its own bean; the calculator receives all of them as a List, in @Order. Factors hold no per-quote
 * state: they are singletons shared by every request at once.
 */
interface PremiumFactor {

    record Step(String factor, String note, long totalPaise) {
    }

    Step apply(Trip trip, long totalPaise);
}

src/main/java/com/bimaly/premiums/Rounding.java

Two beans of one type: nearest rupee (@Primary) and up to the rupee (@Qualifier("premium")).

package com.bimaly.premiums;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Qualifier;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Primary;

/** Two ways to round paise to whole rupees. Two beans of one type: @Primary is the default, @Qualifier picks the other. */
@FunctionalInterface
interface Rounding {

    long toRupee(long paise);

    @Configuration
    class Beans {

        /** The default: nearest rupee, for figures we only display. */
        @Bean
        @Primary
        Rounding nearestRupee() {
            return paise -> Math.round(paise / 100.0) * 100;
        }

        /** The insurer's rule for what is charged: always up to the next rupee, never down. */
        @Bean
        @Qualifier("premium")
        Rounding upToRupee() {
            return paise -> Math.ceilDiv(paise, 100) * 100;
        }
    }
}

package com.bimaly.premiums;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.runner.ApplicationContextRunner;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Primary;

import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

/** The first test written for this station: it reproduces both ways the old wiring went wrong. */
class FactorOrderTrapTest {

    static final Trip SENIOR_IN_EUROPE = new Trip(67, Trip.Destination.EUROPE, 10, true);

    /** The "before" quote service: one factor, injected by type. Kept only in tests. */
    record OldQuoteService(PremiumFactor factor) {
        long quote(Trip trip) {
            return factor.apply(trip, 0).totalPaise();
        }
    }

    @Configuration
    static class TwoFactorsOneConsumer {
        @Bean
        PremiumFactor base() {
            return new Factors.Base();
        }

        @Bean
        PremiumFactor age() {
            return new Factors.Age();
        }

        @Bean
        OldQuoteService oldQuoteService(PremiumFactor factor) {
            return new OldQuoteService(factor);
        }
    }

    @Configuration
    static class SomeoneAddedPrimary {
        @Bean
        PremiumFactor base() {
            return new Factors.Base();
        }

        @Bean
        @Primary
        PremiumFactor age() {
            return new Factors.Age();
        }

        @Bean
        OldQuoteService oldQuoteService(PremiumFactor factor) {
            return new OldQuoteService(factor);
        }
    }

    static long applyInOrder(List<PremiumFactor> factors, Trip trip) {
        long total = 0;
        for (PremiumFactor f : factors) {
            total = f.apply(trip, total).totalPaise();
        }
        return total;
    }

    @Test
    void oneInjectedFactorAmongSeveralStopsTheAppStarting() {
        new ApplicationContextRunner().withUserConfiguration(TwoFactorsOneConsumer.class)
                .run(context -> assertThat(context).hasFailed().getFailure().rootCause().isInstanceOf(NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.class));
    }

    @Test
    void theQuickFixWithPrimaryStartsAndQuotesWithOneFactorOnly() {
        new ApplicationContextRunner().withUserConfiguration(SomeoneAddedPrimary.class).run(context -> {
            assertThat(context).hasNotFailed();
            assertThat(context.getBean(OldQuoteService.class).quote(SENIOR_IN_EUROPE)).isZero();   // age x nothing: a free policy
        });
    }

    @Test
    void theOrderOfTheFactorsChangesThePrice() {
        List<PremiumFactor> right = List.of(new Factors.Base(), new Factors.DestinationRisk(), new Factors.Age(), new Factors.AdventureSports(), new Factors.Minimum());
        List<PremiumFactor> scanned = List.of(new Factors.Base(), new Factors.DestinationRisk(), new Factors.AdventureSports(), new Factors.Age(), new Factors.Minimum());
        assertThat(applyInOrder(right, SENIOR_IN_EUROPE)).isEqualTo(183_875);
        assertThat(applyInOrder(scanned, SENIOR_IN_EUROPE)).isEqualTo(223_875);   // the adventure loading multiplied by age: Rs 400 more
    }
}

package com.bimaly.premiums;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Qualifier;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.runner.ApplicationContextRunner;
import org.springframework.context.ConfigurableApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.core.annotation.Order;

import java.lang.reflect.Modifier;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

/** How the beans are wired: the list's order, which rounding is which, scopes, and the startup check. */
@SpringBootTest
class FactorWiringTest {

    @Autowired
    List<PremiumFactor> factors;
    @Autowired
    @Qualifier("premium")
    Rounding premiumRounding;
    @Autowired
    Rounding defaultRounding;
    @Autowired
    ConfigurableApplicationContext context;

    @Test
    void theListComesInOrderOrder() {
        // a subsequence, not the exact list: a new factor may slot in between without breaking this test
        assertThat(factors).extracting(f -> f.getClass().getSimpleName())
                .containsSubsequence("Base", "DestinationRisk", "Age", "AdventureSports", "Minimum");
    }

    @Test
    void theQualifiedRoundingRoundsUpAndThePrimaryRoundsToNearest() {
        assertThat(premiumRounding.toRupee(106_301)).isEqualTo(106_400);
        assertThat(defaultRounding.toRupee(106_301)).isEqualTo(106_300);
    }

    @Test
    void factorsAreStatelessSingletons() {
        for (String name : context.getBeanNamesForType(PremiumFactor.class)) {
            assertThat(context.getBeanFactory().getBeanDefinition(name).isSingleton()).as(name).isTrue();
            Class<?> type = context.getBean(name).getClass();
            assertThat(Arrays.stream(type.getDeclaredFields()).filter(f -> !Modifier.isStatic(f.getModifiers())))
                    .as(type.getSimpleName() + " keeps no per-quote state").isEmpty();
        }
    }

    @Order(30)
    static class SecondAgeFactor implements PremiumFactor {
        public Step apply(Trip trip, long total) {
            return new Step("age again", "", total);
        }
    }

    @Test
    void twoFactorsWithTheSameOrderStopTheAppStarting() {
        new ApplicationContextRunner()
                .withUserConfiguration(Rounding.Beans.class, Factors.Base.class, Factors.Age.class, SecondAgeFactor.class, PremiumCalculator.class)
                .run(ctx -> assertThat(ctx).hasFailed().getFailure().rootCause()
                        .isInstanceOf(IllegalStateException.class).hasMessageContaining("shares @Order(30)"));
    }
}

package com.bimaly.premiums;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
class PremiumQuoteController {

    /** Oldest age we quote online (a demo rule); older travellers are referred to an agent. */
    static final int MAX_ONLINE_AGE = 80;

    record QuoteRequest(@NotNull @Min(0) @Max(120) Integer age, @NotNull Trip.Destination destination,
                        @NotNull @Min(1) @Max(180) Integer days, Boolean adventureSports, Boolean preExistingCondition) {
        // Boolean, not boolean: the field is optional, and Jackson 3 rejects a missing primitive (FAIL_ON_NULL_FOR_PRIMITIVES)
    }

    private final PremiumCalculator calculator;

    PremiumQuoteController(PremiumCalculator calculator) {
        this.calculator = calculator;
    }

    /** A quote only: no policy is issued and nothing is charged. */
    @PostMapping("/premium-quotes")
    PremiumCalculator.Quote quote(@Valid @RequestBody QuoteRequest r) {
        if (r.age() > MAX_ONLINE_AGE) {
            ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                    "Online quotes cover travellers up to " + MAX_ONLINE_AGE + ". An agent can quote for older travellers.");
            p.setTitle("No online cover for this age");
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, p, null);
        }
        return calculator.quote(new Trip(r.age(), r.destination(), r.days(), Boolean.TRUE.equals(r.adventureSports()),
                Boolean.TRUE.equals(r.preExistingCondition())));
    }
}

A Foundations station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

Fail fast
A wrong factor order is a wrong price for every customer. The startup check turns it into a deployment that never starts, which is far cheaper.
Scopes
Factors are singletons shared by all requests at once, so they hold no per-quote state. Anything per quote lives in local variables or the returned breakdown.
Explainability
The breakdown shows every step. Customers and regulators ask "why this price?"; the answer is in the response.
Money
Paise throughout, rounded per step and once more at the end, up, as the insurer's rule says.

Interview takeaways

What happens when you inject one bean and several exist?

Spring fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException. Fix it by injecting a List of all of them, or choosing one with @Qualifier; @Primary only sets a default.

In what order does Spring inject a List of beans?

Sorted by @Order or the Ordered interface when present. Without them the order is not specified, so never rely on it.

@Qualifier or @Primary?

@Primary marks the default for anyone who does not ask for a specific one. @Qualifier asks for a specific one. Use both: a sensible default, and explicit choices where it matters.

What is the default bean scope, and what follows?

Singleton: one instance shared by every request. So beans must not keep per-request state in fields.

What is @PostConstruct for?

Code that runs once after injection, before the bean is used: a good place to validate configuration and fail at startup.

Self-check rubric

AreaMeets the barAbove the bar
